title: Innovation capacity is concentrating in metropolitan ecosystems even as breakthrough technology advances coexist with slower investment growth
source_unit: WIPO, Global Innovation Index 2025: Innovation at a Crossroads
geography: 139 economies and global science-and-technology innovation clusters, including cross-border metropolitan regions

observations.period: 2025 Global Innovation Index; economy-level innovation systems

denominator.unit: economies assessed in the Global Innovation Index 2025

leading_economies.value: Switzerland, Sweden, United States, Republic of Korea, Singapore, United Kingdom, Finland, Netherlands, Denmark, and China occupy the top ten

innovation_system_direction.value: AI and quantum technologies advance rapidly while innovation-investment growth slows, venture-capital activity moderates, and patenting gains remain modest

measurement_scope.value: investment patterns, technological progress, adoption rates, and socioeconomic impacts

observations.method: WIPO composite index and tracker using innovation inputs and outputs, investment patterns, technological progress, adoption, and socioeconomic-impact indicators across 139 economies.
observations.uncertainty: A composite ranking depends on indicator selection, imputation, weights, time lags, and cross-country data quality. It does not identify causal effects of innovation policy, explain within-country inequality, or equate rank with broad social welfare.
observations.subgroup: Economies by income and region, national innovation systems, firms, universities, inventors, workers, investors, and communities affected by technology diffusion.
observations.counterinterpretation: Slower aggregate investment growth can coexist with high-value breakthroughs or diffusion in particular sectors; a lower-ranked economy may generate important innovation not captured equally by the index.

observations.period: 2025 innovation-cluster ranking; patents, publications, and venture capital

denominator.unit: top 100 global innovation clusters ranked by combined science, patent, and venture-capital activity

top_100_pct_share.unit: approximately percent of global PCT filings and venture-capital deal activity represented by the top 100 clusters

top_100_publication_share.unit: approximately percent of global scientific publications represented by the top 100 clusters

top_10_concentration.value: about 40% of PCT filings, 35% of venture-capital deal activity, and more than 15% of global scientific publications

observations.method: WIPO bottom-up, data-driven cluster method using the geographic density and global share of inventors, scientific authors, patent filings, and venture-capital deals, with VC added as a metric in 2025.
observations.uncertainty: Cluster boundaries can cross municipal, subnational, or national borders; patent, publication, and VC measures capture different innovation stages and may overrepresent formal, investable, or internationally visible activity. Concentration is not ownership or benefit incidence.
observations.subgroup: Metropolitan regions, cross-border corridors, universities, R&D firms, startups, venture investors, public research systems, and local labour and housing markets.
observations.counterinterpretation: Cluster concentration can support knowledge spillovers, specialized infrastructure, and global collaboration, while innovation may diffuse beyond cluster boundaries or arise in less VC-intensive forms.

observations.period: 2025 innovation-cluster ranking; national and regional concentration

denominator.unit: top 100 global innovation clusters and represented economies

us_clusters.unit: top-100 clusters associated with the United States

middle_income_presence.value: clusters from Brazil, Egypt, India, Iran, Malaysia/Singapore, Mexico, and Türkiye appear in the top 100

cross_border_unit.value: many clusters span municipal, sub-federal, or national borders

observations.method: WIPO cluster ranking and economy-level mapping, including cross-border cluster identification and intensity measures normalized by population.
observations.uncertainty: Cluster affiliation and counts are sensitive to methodology, data availability, and the inclusion of venture-capital activity. Presence in the top 100 does not establish equal regional access, local employment, public revenue, or community benefit.
observations.subgroup: Countries, metropolitan regions, middle-income economies, cross-border innovation corridors, and local populations exposed to concentrated investment and talent demand.
observations.counterinterpretation: A geographically concentrated ecosystem can coexist with distributed production, remote collaboration, public research, and innovation outside formal cluster rankings; concentration is a structural signal, not a complete account of innovation opportunity.

related_sources.claim: WIPO ranking and economy-level GII 2025 results.
WIPO companion release on leaders, investment slowdown, and innovation-system findings.

boundary: This record adds innovation-system and cluster-concentration evidence to the firm, infrastructure, work, and geopolitical map. It is not firm-level causal evidence, does not estimate local distribution or household outcomes, and does not establish that innovation concentration produces or reduces inequality, political legitimacy, or state power.
